correctness.rationale: Every assumption and branch of the shortest-path formula is specified: for angular separation larger than the sum of radial tangent angles, path length is g(rho)+g(sigma)+r theta. The strictly increasing g and theta locate the maximal pair at opposite points of the outer circle and yield the exact diameter. The radial density and uniformly distributed smaller polar angle determine probability normalization. Fixed-positive-hole local Taylor expansion gives the three-simplex volume 1/6 and cubic constant 2R^4/(3 pi r (R^2-r^2)^3). With r=a sqrt(R epsilon), the two path branches yield angular defects F_a(z)=a z for z<=2a and a^2+z^2/4 otherwise; integrating the limiting triangular radial sections yields the explicitly checked J(a). At a=0 the disk coefficient follows. Monotonicity at fixed K proves reconstruction; dominated convergence follows from localization to outer antipodal endpoints and coercive local angular and radial deficits. The packaged quadrature verifier passes 18 finite examples; symbolic integration confirms J(a). The universal result rests on the analytic proof, not finite numerics.

value.rationale: This gives an exact and geometrically motivated singular-perturbation mechanism in a canonical nonconvex length space: a positive circular obstacle makes farthest-distance upper tails cubic, while a zero-radius hole gives exponent 5/2. The critical sqrt(R epsilon) scale has a nontrivial, explicitly piecewise crossover with a named endpoint threshold and marked conditional law; these recover the full geometry from distance-distribution extremes. The finding is not simply recomputation of ambient chord moments or an arbitrary numerical slice.
